q: In general, most of the electrical energy supplied to a resistor in an electric circuit is converted into heat.
e: Resistors are specifically designed to dissipate electrical energy primarily as heat.

q: The heating effect of electric current has special applications in domestic appliances.
e: Many household devices rely on this heating effect for their primary function.

q: An electric light bulb is made of a glass bulb consisting a copper filament.
e: An electric light bulb is made of a glass bulb consisting of a tungsten filament.

q: A small amount of oxygen, an active gas, is added after the air is removed from the light bulb.
e: A small amount of argon, an inert gas, is added after the air is removed from the light bulb.

q: The tungsten filament becomes hot when a current flows through it.
e: The resistance of the filament causes it to heat up significantly as current passes through.

q: The inert gas increases the evaporation of the filament.
e: The inert gas reduces the evaporation of the filament.

q: The electric light bulb converts most of the electrical energy into heat and light energy.
e: Incandescent bulbs are highly inefficient, converting the majority of their input energy into heat rather than light.

q: In an electric iron, a mica sheet is wound around the nichrome wire.
e: Mica acts as an insulating framework to hold and isolate the heating element.

q: Mica is a good electrical conductor and can withstand very high temperature.
e: Mica is a good electrical insulator and can withstand very high temperature.

q: The heating element in an electric iron is controlled by a thermostat.
e: The thermostat regulates the temperature by managing the power to the heating element.

q: The thermostat switches the current on and off to maintain the selected temperature.
e: This cycling action keeps the iron at a steady, user-defined heat level.

q: An electric iron has an electric power of $15-45 	ext{ W}$.
e: An electric iron has an electric power of $750-1000 	ext{ W}$.

q: In an electric stove, a coil of nichrome wire is placed in the groove of the heat-resistant material.
e: Nichrome is used because of its high resistance and ability to withstand high heating temperatures.

q: An electric stove has an electrical power ranging from $600 	ext{ W}$ to $2000 	ext{ W}$.
e: This high power range is necessary to generate sufficient heat for cooking.

q: A laptop computer typically has an electrical power of $100-250 	ext{ W}$.
e: A laptop computer typically has an electrical power of $15-45 	ext{ W}$.

q: A refrigerator typically has an electrical power of $100-250 	ext{ W}$.
e: This is the standard operating power range for typical household refrigerators.

q: A fuse is a thin short wire of tin-lead alloy.
e: This specific alloy is chosen for its low melting point, allowing it to break the circuit easily.

q: A fuse is used in electric circuits to prevent electrical appliances from being damaged if excessive current flows through them.
e: The fuse acts as a sacrificial safety device to protect the rest of the circuit.

q: The fuse wire is fitted in a glass tube (cartridge) or on a porcelain block.
e: These housings safely contain the fuse wire and any arcing that occurs when it melts.

q: When a current greater than the rated value flows in the circuit, the fuse becomes so hot that it will melt and break the circuit.
e: The heat generated by the excessive current ($I^2Rt$) melts the fuse wire, opening the circuit.

q: For an appliance rated as $700 	ext{ W}$ or less, a $13 	ext{ A}$ fuse should be fitted.
e: For an appliance rated as $700 	ext{ W}$ or less, a $3 	ext{ A}$ fuse should be fitted.

q: For appliances above $700 	ext{ W}$, a $13 	ext{ A}$ fuse should be fitted.
e: Higher wattage appliances draw more current and therefore require a higher-rated fuse.

q: When the fuse melts, the current stops flowing and the electrical appliance in the circuit is not damaged.
e: By breaking the circuit, the fuse prevents overheating and potential fire or damage to the appliance.
